verdict: AMD's revenue rose 24% to a record $7.7B as Data Center sales jumped 69% on AI chips, but a $186M restructuring charge and an unusually heavy tax bill held GAAP profit to $482M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $0.41 a year ago; non-GAAP EPS was $1.09

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: EPYC server processors and Instinct AI accelerators — a record $3.9B, up 69% on the strong ramp of Instinct GPU shipments and growth in EPYC sales.

segments.name: Client
segments.note: Ryzen processors for PCs — a record $2.3B, up 58% on strong demand for Ryzen processors.

segments.name: Gaming
segments.note: Graphics cards and console chips — down 59% YoY as semi-custom console chip sales fell.

segments.name: Embedded
segments.note: Chips built into cars, industrial gear and communications equipment (the Xilinx business) — down 13% as customers kept working through their inventories.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next generations of CPUs, GPUs and AI accelerators.

opex.name: Marketing, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Writing down the value of technology bought in acquisitions (Xilinx above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash.

opex.name: Restructuring & other
opex.note: Restructuring charges of $186M, partly offset by an $11M licensing gain.

otherDetail: Other income of $37M, plus $12M of equity income and less $19M of interest expense — a net +$30M.
footerNote: Cost of sales of $3,776M includes $252M of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, following AMD's own presentation of its income statement.

takeaways.title: Data Center set the pace
takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit a record $3.9B, up 69%, as Instinct AI GPU shipments ramped and EPYC server CPUs kept growing — the segment is now half of everything AMD sells.

takeaways.title: PC chips had a record quarter too
takeaways.text: Client revenue was a record $2.3B, up 58% on Ryzen demand — together, Data Center and Client growth more than covered a 59% drop in Gaming and a 13% dip in Embedded.

takeaways.title: Taxes ate the profit growth
takeaways.text: Operating income more than doubled to $871M, yet net income fell to $482M from $667M a year ago: a $419M tax provision — a 47% effective rate — plus the $186M restructuring charge absorbed the gains. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.09.

oneTimers: Restructuring charges of $186M — one-off costs of reshaping the business, shown in the 'Restructuring & other' line net of an $11M licensing gain.

GAAP results carry $584M of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles ($252M in cost of sales and $332M in operating expenses) — bookkeeping from past deals, not cash. On AMD's non-GAAP view, EPS was $1.09 instead of $0.29.
